title: Contract-aware deprecation playbook for legacy long-poll and bulk-generate endpoints
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines a contract-aware, phased deprecation and migration plan for two legacy surface areas: the long-poll streaming transport (legacy longpoll/v0-stream endpoints) and the bulk-generate batch HTTP endpoints. Customers with contractual commitments or custom integrations will receive a tailored migration corridor including a temporary compatibility bridge, migration credits, and explicit SLAs for remediation support.

Background / Problem:
- Legacy transports and bulk endpoints are maintenance and security burdens for the platform runtime and block routing/optimization improvements (prefix caching and modern batching).
- Previous deprecation playbooks focused on general migration guidance but did not embed contractual obligations or provide an automated compatibility shim for high-value customers.

Goals:
- Provide a clear, legally-aware timeline that satisfies enterprise contract constraints.
- Offer a short-term compatibility bridge (managed proxy) that translates legacy bulk/longpoll calls to the unified streaming/generate API for a maximum of 9 months after GA of the bridge.
- Deliver SDK/tooling and a CLI-assisted migration path to reduce manual work for customers.
- Ensure telemetry and billing accurately report legacy usage, migration progress, and any credits applied.

Non-goals:
- No long-term support for legacy transports beyond the bridge window.
- No changes to model behavior or alignment guarantees as part of this project.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Maya Thompson (owner), Elliot Park (PM lead)
- Eng: Runtime team (kernel/batching), API team, Infra (compat proxy), SDK team
- Legal & Contracts: Priya Desai
- Support & Success: Diego Chen
- Sales & AE escalation: Hannah Leung

Deliverables:
- Contract-aware timeline spreadsheet and templated amendment language for legal (docs/contract-amendments).
- Compatibility bridge (managed proxy) with limited traffic quota and deprecation telemetry.
- SDK updates: client-side migration helper and opt-in compatibility toggle.
- CLI migration assistant for bulk-to-batched requests and example conversion scripts.
- Support runbook and escalation matrix.
- Telemetry dashboards and migration health signals.

Billing / Credits:
- Tiered migration credit scheme: 3 months full credits for customers with >$X committed ARR or formal contractual clause; 50% credits for next 3 months for mid-size customers; self-serve customers receive 1 month of onboarding credits. Finance and Legal to approve final thresholds.

Acceptance Criteria Summary (see field 'acceptance_criteria' for detail):
- All enterprise customers with contractual clauses receive written amendment offer and access to the compatibility bridge within 14 days of notice.
- Compatibility bridge successfully translates legacy semantics for 95% of calls observed in pilot customers.
- SDK helper and CLI reduce manual migration time by >=50% in pilot.
- Telemetry captures legacy endpoint usage, migration state, and any error regressions; dashboards are live pre-notice.

Risks and Mitigations:
- Risk: Proxy introduces latency. Mitigation: soft-rate-limit bridge usage and provide per-customer latency SLOs; recommend in-contract SLAs.
- Risk: Customers rely on undefined legacy behaviors. Mitigation: compatibility testing harness + automated warning logs enumerating unsupported patterns.
- Risk: Legal approval delays. Mitigation: early engagement with contracts team; use templated amendment language for rapid sign-off.

Operational Runbook Highlights:
- Bridge onboarding flow for AE/SE: request -> entitlement -> onboarding runbook -> 7-day pilot -> migrate -> decommission legacy on agreed date.
- Rollback: if excessive errors, route customer back to legacy pool for 72 hours and triage; escalation to oncall infra and runtime leads.

Telemetry & Dashboards:
- Metrics to track: legacy_request_rate, bridge_translation_success_rate, average_latency_delta, migration_completion_percentage, credits_applied_count, customer_error_rate.
- Dashboards required: per-customer migration status, platform-wide legacy usage heatmap, contract-bound customer list.

Communication Plan:
- Week 0: Private notices to impacted contractual customers and AE/SE packets.
- Week 2: Public deprecation announcement in docs + blog post with migration resources.
- Ongoing: Weekly migration digest for internal stakeholders and weekly customer migration status updates for enterprise AEs.

Post-deprecation:
- After bridge end-of-life, customers still on legacy will be rate-limited and billed at a premium until migrated or contractually exempted.
- Run a 30-day post-deprecation health review and produce a migration retrospective.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Contract comms: All customers with an active contract clause receive amendment language and a named AE engagement plan within 14 days of plan approval.
2) Bridge readiness: Compatibility bridge deployed to staging and passes synthetic translation tests covering 95% of legacy call patterns in pilot.
3) SDK/CLI: SDK migration helper and CLI conversion tool published in SDK repo with example conversions and unit tests.
4) Metrics: Dashboards for legacy usage and migration progress live prior to public notice.
5) Support: Support runbook and escalation matrix published and training session completed for Support/Success.
6) Decommission gating: Final decommission only allowed when migration_completion_percentage >= 90% for contract-bound customers, or explicit contract amendment exists.
7) Legal: Amendment template approved by Legal and Finance.
8) Pricing/Credits: Migration credit policy signed off by Finance.
migration_mapping:
Legacy surface => Migration path notes:
- /v0/longpoll/stream -> migrate clients to streaming websocket or SSE via /v1/streaming. For customers unable to change, enable compatibility bridge that maintains per-connection semantics but translates to multiple streaming connections on the backend. Bridge limited to 200 concurrent legacy connections per customer.
- /v0/bulk/generate -> recommend batch-invoke of unified /v1/generate with batchable prompts. Provide code samples and a CLI tool to chunk/merge payloads. For customers with very large payloads that exceed current backend limits, offer temporary elevated payload quotas during migration window.
- Model aliasing: Where model aliases differ, bridge maps alias -> recommended current model with best-effort shim for legacy parameters. Document behavioral diffs in compatibility report.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Prep, 6 weeks): Legal templates, dashboard build, compatibility bridge prototype, SDK helper draft.
Phase 1 (Private pilot, 4 weeks): Invite 3 strategic contract-bound customers, enable bridge, instrument metrics, iterate SDK.
Phase 2 (Contracted rollouts, 8-12 weeks): Onboard AE-organized customers, offer migration credits, run migrations.
Phase 3 (Public Notice & Opt-in, 4 weeks): Publish deprecation timeline and tooling to all customers; allow self-serve bridge enablement for a limited quota.
Phase 4 (Enforcement & Decommission, after bridge window ends): Begin premium rate limiting for non-migrated, complete decommission per contract schedule.
monitoring_signals:
- legacy_request_rate (per-customer)
- bridge_translation_success_rate >= 95%
- average_latency_delta < 150ms for proxyed calls
- migration_completion_percentage per contract cohort
- customer_error_rate and 5xx trend
- support tickets tagged 'legacy-migration'
communication_plan:
- Legal & AE packet: templated amendment + migration checklist (private).
- Docs: Detailed migration guide and 'how-to' for SDKs, with code examples and CLI walkthrough.
- Blog + changelog: Public timeline, FAQ, and post-mortem policy.
- In-product: banner for impacted org admins with direct link to migration console.
open_questions: What exact thresholds for 'committed ARR' qualify a customer for the 3-month full credits? (Finance decision)
Does the contracts team require a formal signed amendment for every enterprise customer or is an AE email ack sufficient?
What hard cap do we set on bridge concurrency per org to control cost exposure?
